📝 In the event of a prolonged conflict involving Iran and its regional or Western adversaries, strategic and operational objectives generally revolve around a logic of progressively degrading the adversary’s military capabilities while limiting escalation toward a full-scale regional war. The campaign would not necessarily aim at territorial conquest, but rather at a lasting modification of the military and strategic balance in the Middle East. The central strategic objective would be to prevent Iran from maintaining or expanding its power-projection capabilities—whether through ballistic missiles, drones, paramilitary networks, or a potentially weaponizable nuclear program. Within this framework, the operational level of warfare focuses on producing concrete military effects that support the political objective. A sustained air and naval campaign would first seek to neutralize Iranian air defense systems in order to open the airspace and enable deep strikes against military infrastructure. The destruction or neutralization of missile bases, weapons depots, command centers, and arms-production facilities would be a major objective. The underlying idea is to reduce Iran’s ability to conduct long-range strikes against military bases, energy infrastructure, or urban centers across the region. At the same time, naval forces would aim to secure critical maritime routes in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz in order to prevent major disruptions to global energy trade. Another essential dimension of the strategy involves containing networks of allied forces or proxies supported by Iran, particularly those linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. These networks, present in several Middle Eastern countries, allow Tehran to exercise indirect military influence and maintain constant pressure on its adversaries. The operational objective is therefore to reduce the ability of these groups to act in a coordinated manner or to receive material and financial resources. This involves monitoring and disrupting supply routes, applying diplomatic and economic pressure on the financial networks that support them, and conducting targeted operations against logistical infrastructure and command centers that enable them to operate. In this context, the containment strategy is not limited to military operations. It also includes political, economic, and informational dimensions. Sanctions, diplomatic pressure, and cooperation with regional partner states aim to isolate the structures that support these networks and reduce their room for maneuver. At the same time, intelligence operations play a central role in identifying supply chains, financial circuits, and organizational structures that enable proxy forces to function. The ultimate objective is to fragment these networks and deprive them of the ability to operate as instruments of regional power projection. The potential duration of a campaign lasting several weeks or months can be explained by the dispersed and resilient nature of Iran’s military capabilities. Infrastructure is often spread across a vast territory and protected by defensive measures or concealment strategies. A military campaign must therefore progress through successive phases: suppression of air defenses, neutralization of major offensive capabilities, and then the degradation of command structures and logistical networks. This process requires time, as it involves a combination of military strikes, intelligence collection, and continuous assessment of the effects produced. Finally, an implicit strategic objective is to maintain the regional balance while avoiding uncontrolled escalation. The actors involved aim to achieve their military objectives while avoiding a broader regional war. Each year, reopening Going-to-the-Sun Road in Glacier National Park depends on daily avalanche forecasting and a decades-long partnership between the U.S. Geological Survey and the National Park Service. The 50-mile engineering marvel crosses the Continental Divide, connecting the east and west sides of the park. Since 2003, USGS avalanche scientists have worked side-by-side with the NPS to deliver daily avalanche forecasts that guide “go/no-go” decisions for crews clearing snow and avalanche debris from the road. Spring conditions in Glacier can change quickly, with sudden snowstorms and avalanches threatening crew safety and slowing progress. This USGS–NPS partnership ensures road crews have the information they need to work safely and efficiently, saving time and resources while helping the park prepare for the busy season ahead. The Going-to-the-Sun Road typically opens in late June or early July each year. Visitors can check the park’s website for the latest updates. Video

We've been reviewing photos of the dust covered bodies of children and verifying their names against the names scrawled on little coffins. We've been debunking false claims about the attack and that the harrowing cemetery photo isn't real. And while it appeared obvious to many early on that the U.S. or Israel hit the school, it takes days to sift through, pinpoint and analyze the evidence. It took four days before a new satellite image we ordered came through so we could confidently assess the damage and the types of weapons used. All that reporting and cross checking and the production of the visuals showing it takes time. But it ultimately allows us to more confidently assert U.S. responsibility, explain our rationale and add to the body of reporting that officials should be challenged with. 🇰🇼🇺🇸 | Le Koweït a commencé à réduire la production de certains champs pétroliers après avoir atteint la limite de ses capacités de stockage, selon des personnes proches du dossier. Cela intervient alors que la fermeture du détroit d’Ormuz paralyse les exportations. Le pays envisage de nouvelles réductions de production, pouvant aller jusqu’à ne produire que ce qui est nécessaire pour la consommation domestique. Une décision est attendue dans les prochains jours. Les installations de stockage dans tout le Golfe se remplissent rapidement. Selon la société de données Kpler, l’Arabie saoudite et les Émirats arabes unis devraient atteindre leurs limites de stockage en moins de trois semaines. Une fois les capacités de stockage saturées, les producteurs risquent de devoir arrêter complètement la production, une opération coûteuse qui peut endommager les puits pétroliers. (WSJ)

During a meeting with the warriors of the 12th Special Forces Brigade Azov of the National Guard of Ukraine, I awarded the defenders with the Order of Bohdan Khmelnytsky, the Order “For Courage,” and the Order of Danylo Halytskyi, and presented the shoulder boards of a brigadier general to Denys Prokopenko. Thank you for defending our state since the first days of the occupation of Crimea and part of our east – Donbas – and throughout all the years of the full-scale war, for your courage. The brigade’s warriors took part in eliminating the Dobropillia breakthrough. They are now defending this sector – holding Rodynske, Bilytske, and Shakhove, and organizing the defense of Dobropillia. We discussed the situation in their area of responsibility, funding for drone capabilities, AWOL cases, evacuation, and the repair of logistics routes. All proposals from the military will be taken into account and promptly addressed.

Across all districts of Punjab, areas prone to ponding, where rainwater accumulates during the rainy season, have been carefully identified. To minimize the risk of urban flooding and to strengthen the capacity of cities to manage stormwater effectively, a landmark initiative has been launched. For the first time in the history of Punjab, 358 Underground Storage Tanks (UGSs), including roadside underground storage systems equipped with recharge wells, are being constructed across the province. This major infrastructure project, with an estimated cost of Rs. 33 billion, will provide a combined storage capacity of approximately 94 million gallons of rainwater. These facilities will not only help mitigate urban flooding during heavy rainfall but will also support groundwater recharge and promote more sustainable water management in our cities. “This is My Sohna Punjab.” Video

It seems highly unlikely that the White House would now settle for the sort of nuclear-only deal that was discussed in the previous two rounds of talks. 2) Conversely, Iran has been attacked twice in the past year. It is navigating its first transition since 1989 under American and Israeli fire. The political incentives right now push the regime toward defiance, not deference. A comprehensive deal in which the regime negotiates away its military capabilities is highly improbable. 3) Even a nuclear-only deal might be a stretch right now, given the number of voices in Iran no doubt arguing that the lesson of the past year is to emulate North Korea. 4) Any deal would likely have to include significant economic benefits for Iran, thus giving the regime the resources to rebuild the very capabilities America and Israel now seek to destroy. 5) For those economic benefits to materialize, Gulf states would have to provide opportunities for trade and investment.
